title: Chicken thigh, sauteed, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh without skin is the meat from the bird's thigh, cooked by sautéing in a pan. Removing the skin reduces fat content while preserving the juiciness and characteristic flavor of the meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thigh meat contains more iron and zinc than chicken breast.
When sautéed without skin, some fat melts away, making the dish less caloric but still flavorful thanks to Maillard reactions.
Chicken thigh is a staple in many world cuisines – from French coq au vin to Asian teriyaki dishes.
Thigh meat is more tender than breast due to higher connective tissue content.
Proper high‑heat sautéing can create a crisp exterior without excess oil.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides high‑quality complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health, metabolism, and skin integrity.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Removing the skin dramatically cuts saturated fat, making it more suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Contains creatine
items.content: Creatine aids cellular energy production in muscles, beneficial for active individuals.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some people are allergic to chicken proteins and may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: If the thighs are marinated, sodium levels can be high, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Histamine formation
items.content: Improper storage can lead to histamine buildup, causing food intolerance symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skinless chicken thighs can be sautéed, braised, baked, or added to salads and soups. Pat the pieces dry before cooking to achieve a golden crust. Serve with vegetables, whole grains, or your favorite sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw thighs refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days, or freeze in airtight bags for up to 6 months. Cooked meat lasts 3‑4 days in the fridge. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
